\begin{tablenotes}[flushleft]
\footnotesize
\item \textit{Notes:} The 15:30 forecast of the closing half hour (the 16:00 bar) of the pooled models of Table~\ref{tab:rh_oos}, scored against the actual realized variance $\RV_t$ of the closing half hour, one forecast a day. Panel~A: the $\rhcaNdaysSpan$ evaluation days of Table~\ref{tab:rh_oos}; Panel~B: $\mathcal T_{\mathrm{oos}}$, the days of Section~\ref{sec:rh_results_predictors}, with the models trained on the closing half hour only (Table~\ref{tab:rh_oos_last30}). HAR: HAR benchmark; Full: full predictor set; on the HAR benchmark the pooled ridge, lasso and elastic net reproduce the OLS forecast (Section~\ref{sec:rh_exp_setup}). MSE in units of $10^{-\rhcaMseExp}$. $R^2_{\mathrm{OOS}}$ against the historical mean of the closing-half-hour realized variance from \rhoosBenchStart{} \citep{CampbellThompson2008}. Full vs HAR: $\Delta\% = 100(\bar L^{\mathrm{Full}}/\bar L^{\mathrm{HAR}} - 1)$ for the mean QLIKE of the same model; vs closing HAR: the same change against the closing-interval HAR benchmark ($^{a}$, the OLS on the HAR benchmark estimated on the closing half hour, Appendix~\ref{app:rh_closing_bench}), which has no forecast before \rhcaCloseFirst{} (--: not available on Panel~A's span); the closing-interval ridge, lasso and elastic net on the HAR benchmark are within \rhcaCiHarGapBound\% of it. $\DM$: Diebold--Mariano statistic of the daily QLIKE differential (Harvey--Leybourne--Newbold, $q_{\mathrm{NW}} = \rhcaDMLagSpan$ in Panel~A and \rhcaDMLagOos{} in Panel~B); negative: the first forecast has the lower loss. $^{*}$, $^{**}$, $^{***}$: significance at the 10\%, 5\% and 1\% levels. The penalized linear models' full-set changes differ between the panels because the two halves of Panel~A's span disagree: on \rhcaYearsPre{} the full set lowers their closing-half-hour QLIKE ($\Delta\% = \rhcaPctRidgeClosePre$, \rhcaPctLassoClosePre{} and \rhcaPctEnetClosePre{} for ridge, lasso and elastic net; $\DM = \rhcaDmRidgeClosePre$, \rhcaDmLassoClosePre{} and \rhcaDmEnetClosePre), on $\mathcal T_{\mathrm{oos}}$ it raises it, and over the whole span the two offset.
\end{tablenotes}
